title: Fixed Asset Register Updater
summary: Upload your existing Fixed Asset Register, this period's Fixed Asset GL entries, and any invoices you have, and get back an updated FAR workbook: new additions are added without duplicates, and depreciation, accumulated depreciation and NBV are rolled forward for every asset - old and new - for the period. A Needs Review sheet flags anything that needs a human look (missing invoices, unmatched GL rows, or category totals that don't tie to the GL). Your original FAR file is never changed.
prompt: Develop a Fixed Asset Register automation feature that updates our existing FAR based on new additions posted in the relevant Fixed Asset GLs. We will also provide the relevant invoices, and the system should use the invoices to capture the proper asset description, invoice date, vendor, invoice number and other relevant details. The system should identify new additions from the GLs and add them to the existing FAR without duplication. Along with adding new assets, the system should also automatically update the depreciation of all existing assets already included in the FAR for the relevant period, as well as calculate depreciation for the newly added assets from their applicable depreciation start date. The Fixed Asset Schedule should therefore continuously update the asset cost, depreciation, accumulated depreciation and NBV for both existing and new assets. The FAR and depreciation schedule should be updated based on the GLs and supporting invoices and should reconcile with the relevant GL balances. tHE FILE I ATTACHED USE THAT EXACT FILE FOR THIS FEATURE
assumptions: A GL row is added only when its reference, date, amount and GL account/category all parse and the account maps to an existing category sheet; otherwise it goes to Needs Review rather than being guessed or silently skipped
A new addition's depreciation rate is the rate on the most recently purchased existing asset in that category sheet, never an invented rate
A new addition's first depreciation charge is prorated from its purchase date to the FAR's fiscal year-end, matching the convention already used in the uploaded FAR

Existing assets receive this run's period fraction (period length / 12) of their annual depreciation on top of what is already recorded; if the run crosses into a new fiscal year (detected from the FAR Schedule title versus the period end date), prior-year depreciation is folded in and the current year's depreciation restarts

Cells not touched by this run - including any pre-existing #REF! errors - are left exactly as they were; formula cells that ARE read (e.g. cost, rate) rely on Excel's last-calculated (cached) value, so a workbook that has never been opened/saved in Excel may have unreadable formula cells

Invoice text extraction from PDFs is best-effort pattern matching on embedded text only - no OCR or handwriting recognition; unreadable/scanned invoices are treated as 'no invoice' for that addition, per spec
Each run covers one period (e.g. one month or quarter) of GL additions at a time
gaps: If a GL account/category cannot be matched to any existing FAR category sheet, that addition is flagged on the Needs Review sheet rather than auto-creating a new category sheet
PDF invoice field extraction (invoice number, vendor, description) is heuristic and may need manual correction - the invoice register spreadsheet is the reliable input path
Disposals, write-offs, transfers, revaluations, and posting entries back into an accounting system are out of scope, per the approved spec

Stray total/note rows embedded within a category sheet (not part of the recognised asset-row columns) are pushed down when new rows are inserted rather than recalculated - the authoritative totals are the FAR Schedule summary block this tool generates
expects: Your existing FAR workbook (.xlsx) - the exact file you already maintain, with the 'FAR Schedule' summary sheet and category ledger sheets (Description, Date of Purchase, Cost, Depr. Rate, Opening, Dep for the year, Acc Dep, WDV present as they are today)
This period's Fixed Asset GL entries (.xlsx or .csv) with, at minimum, a date, a unique voucher/transaction reference, the GL account/category, and the amount
Optional: an invoice register (.xlsx/.csv) with invoice number, invoice date, vendor, description and amount for the period's new additions
Optional: raw invoice files (.pdf or .txt) for the period's new additions, if you don't have an invoice register
The period end date, the period length in months, and (optionally) a fiscal year-end override (MM-DD) if it can't be auto-detected from the FAR Schedule sheet's title
